title: The cities managing climate risk by investing in resilience
gist: Oliver Wyman Forum research ranking 1,500 cities argues climate resilience has become a primary determinant of urban business attractiveness, with 45% of CEOs planning supply chain reconfiguration and nearly three-quarters of organizations already hit by weather-driven losses. Bern, Oslo and Gothenburg top the resilience ranking, while flood-exposed manufacturing hubs in China and water-stressed nearshoring winners like Chihuahua face capital flight risk unless they invest in adaptation infrastructure.

themes.theme: Resilience as a city competitiveness metric

insights.claim: Climate resilience has become a key driver of a city's economic competitiveness, according to new research ranking 1,500 cities globally on business attractiveness.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: City-level resilience scores are becoming a screening input for site selection, real estate and municipal debt; track the Oliver Wyman Forum city ranking as a leading indicator of where corporate capex lands.
insights.quote: Climate resilience is now a key driver of a city’s economic competitiveness, according to new research ranking 1,500 cities on business attractiveness.
insights.locator: Climate resilience is now a key driver

insights.claim: Central and northern European cities including Bern, Oslo and Gothenburg currently rank top in climate resilience among 1,500 cities assessed for business attractiveness.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Northern European metros may command a durable premium in commercial real estate, insurance pricing and talent-dependent industries relative to hot or flood-prone peers.
insights.quote: central and northern European destinations like Bern, Oslo and Gothenburg are currently top ranked in climate resilience, while other cities are poised to rise
insights.locator: Ranking the business attractiveness of 1,500 cities

insights.claim: Nearly three-quarters of organizations have already experienced losses or work disruptions from severe weather, per a 2025 global survey by insurer Marsh.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Physical climate loss is now a broad-base operating cost, not a tail risk — expect continued upward pressure on commercial insurance premiums and business-interruption reserves.
insights.quote: Nearly three-quarters of organizations have experienced losses or work disruptions from weather devastation, according to a 2025 global survey by insurer Marsh.
insights.locator: Severe weather is becoming more common

insights.claim: The primary transmission channels from severe weather to corporate P&L are higher insurance costs, work stoppages and water shortages that shutter factories.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Water availability, not just flood or heat, is the underrated shutdown risk for water-intensive manufacturing — screen portfolio companies by facility-level water stress.
insights.quote: This creates issues including higher insurance costs and work stoppages, as well as water shortages that shutter factories.
insights.locator: This creates issues including higher insurance costs

themes.theme: Supply chain reconfiguration and flood-exposed manufacturing

insights.claim: 45% of CEOs are planning to reconfigure their company's supply chains, according to 2026 research from Oliver Wyman Forum.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: A near-majority of large corporates are in play on footprint decisions in 2026 — logistics, industrial park and port infrastructure operators positioned as resilient destinations capture the reallocation.
insights.quote: But 45% of CEOs are planning to reconfigure their company's supply chains, according to 2026 research from Oliver Wyman Forum.
insights.locator: Bolstering supply chains against climate change

insights.claim: More than 40 of China's top 100 manufacturing cities are at high risk of flooding, per Oliver Wyman Forum data.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Roughly 40% of China's manufacturing base carries a flood-exposure discount — a concrete quantification for anyone modelling China-exit or China-stay decisions.
insights.quote: more than 40 of its top 100 manufacturing cities are at high risk of flooding, according to Oliver Wyman Forum data
insights.locator: Chinese cities have an opportunity to lead in Asia

insights.claim: Sustainability and coastal-defence investment by Chinese cities such as Shenzhen may persuade manufacturers to stay in China rather than diversify to lower-cost countries.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Resilience spend is a retention lever against the de-risking narrative; watch whether Chinese municipal adaptation capex slows the pace of announced relocations.
insights.quote: Sustainability investments in places like Shenzhen, which has a coastal defence system, may persuade manufacturers to stay in China rather than diversify to lower-cost countries.
insights.locator: Sustainability investments in places like Shenzhen

insights.claim: The Port of Rotterdam handles roughly 30% of the EU's container traffic and its adaptation strategy proposes raising quays and roads and relocating electricity and telecoms facilities to higher ground.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: A single node carries roughly a third of EU container flow — its adaptation timeline is a systemic European logistics dependency worth tracking directly.
insights.quote: The Port of Rotterdam, for example, is Europe’s largest seaport and accommodates roughly 30% of the EU’s container traffic.
insights.locator: The Port of Rotterdam, for example

insights.claim: Chihuahua, Mexico has benefited from supply chain shifts but is vulnerable to water shortages, easing pressure only partly by using treated wastewater to irrigate green spaces.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Nearshoring winners can inherit a water constraint that caps the durability of the relocation trade — stress-test Mexican industrial exposure on water supply, not just labour cost.
insights.quote: Chihuahua, Mexico, for example, has benefitted from supply chain shifts but is vulnerable to water shortages.
insights.locator: Those cities that are considered a part of companies’ “China plus one”

insights.claim: Singapore's climate resilience plans include sea walls for coastal and flood defence plus mandatory water recycling requirements for new projects in water-intensive industries.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Mandated water recycling creates a regulated demand pool for water treatment and recycling technology vendors in water-intensive industrial permitting.
insights.quote: Singapore’s climate resilience plans, for example, include sea walls for coastal and flood defence and mandatory water recycling requirements for new projects in water-intensive industries to help prevent scarcity.

insights.claim: Johannesburg is planning for its high flood-risk areas to be free of houses, offices and critical infrastructure by 2050.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Managed retreat as formal municipal policy implies long-dated write-downs on assets inside designated flood zones — a template other cities may copy.
insights.quote: in South Africa, Johannesburg is planning for high flood-risk areas to be free of houses, offices and critical infrastructure by 2050
insights.locator: And in South Africa, Johannesburg is planning

insights.claim: Sao Paulo plans to insulate houses with green areas to prevent heat deaths, harvest rainwater and protect against runoff and flash floods.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Green infrastructure is being adopted as a lower-capex substitute for hard engineering in emerging-market megacities — a distinct procurement channel from seawall-scale contracts.
insights.locator: Other cities, like Sao Paulo, Brazil

themes.theme: Liveability, talent migration and public-private financing

insights.claim: Talent migrates away from cities with excess heat and humidity, frequent floods or water shortages toward milder climates and more resilient infrastructure, making resilience a determinant of skilled labour supply.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Climate exposure feeds directly into wage costs and hiring difficulty for talent-intensive sectors including AI engineering — a second-order channel most site-selection models ignore.
insights.quote: Talent often migrates from cities affected by excess heat and humidity, frequent floods or water shortages to areas with milder climates, more resilient infrastructure and easy access to natural surroundings and activities.
insights.locator: Investing in liveability and talent attraction

insights.claim: Gothenburg offers nearly 3,000 square feet of green space per resident and benefits from a Swedish national initiative to decarbonize industry and create jobs.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: A concrete benchmark for liveability-driven talent attraction; pairing municipal green space with national industrial decarbonization funding is the combination that scores highest.
insights.quote: The city offers nearly 3,000 square feet of green space per resident and benefits from a national initiative to decarbonize the industrial sector and create new jobs.

insights.claim: Riyadh uses smart cooling systems and reflective materials to cool buildings and is adding canopies and small green spaces to improve walkability, showing hot-climate cities can substitute technology for temperate geography.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Gulf urban programmes are a growth market for smart cooling, reflective materials and passive-shading products as heat becomes a talent-retention constraint.
insights.locator: Riyadh in Saudi Arabia, for example

insights.claim: Singapore launched a public-private partnership in April 2026 for business climate resilience covering green procurement and sustainable financing, and issued supervisory guidelines requiring financial institutions to manage their own and their portfolios' climate risk.
insights.speaker: Ben Simpfendorfer
insights.so_what: Supervisory guidance pushing portfolio-level climate risk management into Singaporean financial institutions is a concrete regulatory driver of adaptation-linked capital allocation in Asia.
insights.quote: Singapore launched a public-private partnership in April 2026 to help strengthen businesses’ climate resilience in areas like green procurement and sustainable financing, for example.
